cards.text: Midian is beaten, and the Israelites come to Gideon with a BIG offer: “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.” Three generations? That's a job offer for the whole family TREE!

cards.question: The Israelites want Gideon, his son and his grandson to rule over them. What's Gideon's answer?

answers.text: The LORD will rule over you
My son will rule in my place
I will rule until Midian is gone

cards.text: So Gideon won't rule over them, and neither will his son, but he does ask each man for an earring from his plunder. The enemies were Ishmaelites, so those earrings are gold.

cards.question: When Gideon asks each man for an earring, the Israelites grumble and hold on to their plunder.

cards.text: Earring after earring lands on a spread-out garment: 1,700 shekels of gold, plus crescent ornaments, pendants, the purple garments of Midian's kings and the chains off the camels' necks. Even the CAMELS had to hand over their jewelry!

cards.question: Gideon now has all that gold and royal goods. What does he make from it all?
Gideon places his ephod in Ophrah, his hometown. Soon all Israel is ___ it there.
Once all Israel worships Gideon's ephod, it turns out to be a blessing for Gideon and his household.

cards.text: In this way, Midian is down, and it STAYS down. It never raises its head again.

cards.question: With Midian subdued and never raising its head again, the land has ___ for forty years in the days of Gideon.

cards.text: Then Jerubbaal son of Joash, that's Gideon, goes home and settles down. I fought ONE stubborn ball of dough once and needed a WEEK to settle down, and the dough WON.

cards.question: Gideon has seventy sons. Why so many?

cards.text: SEVENTY sons, and I thought six little cookie cutters made my counter CROWDED! And there's one more son, born to Gideon's concubine.
She lives in Shechem, and Gideon names the boy Abimelech. Later, Gideon dies at a ripe old age and is buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah.

cards.question: As soon as Gideon is dead, what do the Israelites do?

cards.text: They even set up Baal-berith as their god. Gideon is BARELY in the tomb, friend.

cards.question: After Gideon dies, the Israelites remember the LORD their God who delivered them from all their enemies on every side.
Gideon did a lot of good for Israel. How do the Israelites treat the house of Jerubbaal after he's gone?

answers.text: They give it land in Ophrah
They make it rich with gold

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend. Keep that apron tied, because this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: The earlier cards establish only that Gideon made an ephod. They give no basis for reasoning that all Israel will worship it rather than guard or melt it, so this blank asks for an unseen detail by guesswork.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never says that the ephod became a snare to Gideon and his household. Marking the blessing statement false establishes only that it was not a blessing, leaving this central consequence of Judges 8:27 untaught before the cards move on.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
